entries.evidence: Query: 'OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization' (owasp.org). Result title 'OWASP Top 10 API Security Risks' at this URL (2023 edition); the API1:2023 page 'Broken Object Level Authorization' (owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization/) was also returned. Result text: BOLA is the most common API flaw, an authorization check is needed on every endpoint that takes an object ID, GUIDs are a supplement.
entries.version: 2023 edition; a newer edition was not seen (query 'OWASP API Security Top 10 new edition 2025 2026' returned only the web Top 10:2025 and GenAI lists)
entries.notes: Names the risk classes used in the W05 role matrix (BOLA object level, BFLA function level, property level). estimate_minutes is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

entries.title: Password Storage - OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
entries.access_note: Public page returned by the search on the provider's domain; no sign-in indicated.
entries.evidence: Query: 'OWASP Cheat Sheet Series Password Storage Cheat Sheet Argon2id scrypt bcrypt PBKDF2' (cheatsheetseries.owasp.org). First result, title 'Password Storage - OWASP Cheat Sheet Series' at this URL; result text: Argon2id first (minimum 19 MiB memory, 2 iterations, parallelism 1), scrypt (2^17, block size 8, parallelism 1), bcrypt for legacy (work factor at least 10, 72-byte input limit), PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 600,000 iterations when FIPS-140 is required; the search metadata showed an old index date.
entries.version: values as shown in the search summary on 2026-11-18; verify on the live page
entries.notes: Source of the parameters for the D24 synthetic-hash comparison; record the page date when you copy any number. Only generated or synthetic passwords and hashes are used, never third-party dumps. estimate_minutes is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

entries.title: hashlib — Secure hashes and message digests — Python 3.15.2 documentation
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search on docs.python.org; no sign-in.
entries.evidence: Query: 'Python hashlib scrypt pbkdf2_hmac documentation password hashing' (docs.python.org). First result, title 'hashlib — Secure hashes and message digests — Python 3.15.2 documentation' at this URL; result text: hashlib.scrypt (RFC 7914, since Python 3.6), hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac, salt of at least 16 bytes from os.urandom, current example 500,000 iterations.
entries.notes: Local tool practice with generated synthetic passwords only: time a fast hash against PBKDF2 and scrypt with the same salt policy. The standard library documents scrypt and pbkdf2_hmac but no Argon2 or bcrypt (not seen in the result), see the argon2-cffi entry. estimate_minutes is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

entries.title: API Reference
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search on argon2-cffi.readthedocs.io; no sign-in. The library is a third-party package.
entries.evidence: Query: 'argon2-cffi documentation PasswordHasher Argon2id parameters' (web search, no domain filter). Result title 'API Reference' at this URL; result text: Argon2id is the choice when unsure, RFC 9106 profiles RFC_9106_LOW_MEMORY and RFC_9106_HIGH_MEMORY, rehash when parameters or defaults change. The 'Choosing Parameters' page (argon2-cffi.readthedocs.io/en/23.1.0/parameters.html) was also returned; sources disagreed on the default values (m=65536,t=3,p=4 in one mirror), so defaults are not recorded.
entries.notes: Third-party package (installation would need a package index; not verified here). If it is unavailable offline, use the standard-library PBKDF2 and scrypt path. The standard: RFC 9106 (rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9106.html, Informational, September 2021, Argon2 version 1.3). estimate_minutes is a registry planning figure sized to the block, not a provider figure.

plan_fact_checks.claim: OWASP WSTG: the stable documented release is 4.2 (plan sections 4 and 16 item 8; Week 5 core sites).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Queries on WSTG v4.2 pages (owasp.org, wstg.owasp.org): the site names 'Latest (development toward 5.0)', 'Stable (currently v4.2)' and v4.2 as the canonical version to cite; the v4.2 release post 'Web Security Testing Guide v4.2 Released' (owasp.org/2020/12/03/wstg-v42-released) was returned. Versioned links are preferred to 'latest'.

plan_fact_checks.claim: WSTG v4.2 contains a JSON Web Token test page (Week 5 expansion point: case-based JWT validation).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'OWASP WSTG v4.2 Testing JSON Web Tokens session management testing': the only JWT page named was '4.6.10 Testing JSON Web Tokens' in the table of contents of the 'latest' version; v4.2 pages returned were 4.6.1 session management schema and 4.6.4 exposed session variables. Use the OWASP JWT cheat sheet and RFC 8725 for JWT validation.

plan_fact_checks.claim: The JWT validation cases (algorithm allow-list, key purpose, expiration, audience) are documented by official sources.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'RFC 8725 JSON Web Token Best Current Practices' (rfc-editor.org, datatracker.ietf.org): RFC 8725 (BCP 225, February 2020) asks libraries to take a permitted algorithm set, to check audience and issuer keys, and to use explicit typ values; the OWASP JSON Web Token cheat sheet tabulates alg, kid, jku, exp, aud and jti. Note: an update draft draft-ietf-oauth-rfc8725bis exists (version -10 seen); publication as an RFC was not confirmed.

plan_fact_checks.claim: OWASP crAPI (github.com/OWASP/crAPI) is a vulnerable-by-design API for controlled Docker use (plan section 4).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'OWASP crAPI completely ridiculous API vulnerable by design': owasp.org/projects/crapi and github.com/OWASP/crAPI describe a deliberately vulnerable API platform that targets the OWASP API Security Top 10; one page notes it skips classic XSS and SQL injection, so XSS exercises on D21 need PortSwigger or Juice Shop.

plan_fact_checks.claim: OWASP Juice Shop at github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop is the local vulnerable web target (plan section 4).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query on Juice Shop releases (github.com): 'Releases · juice-shop/juice-shop · GitHub' lists v20.4.0 as the latest release with artifacts dated 2026-11-08 (search summary); earlier tags v20.1.0 to v20.3.0 were also listed. Verify the version on the page before pinning.

plan_fact_checks.claim: PortSwigger offers XSS, authentication, access control and JWT labs for the Week 5 gate of at least 4 independent labs across client, auth and API classes.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Searches on portswigger.net returned lab pages for XSS (stored, DOM, reflected into attribute), CSRF, JWT (unverified, flawed, weak key, algorithm confusion), authentication (username enumeration, 2FA bypass), access control (user ID, IDOR, method-based), API testing (mass assignment), file upload and deserialization. The gate is reachable with free-account labs.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Password exercise: Argon2id, bcrypt and PBKDF2 are the appropriate password KDFs to compare with fast hashes.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query on the OWASP Password Storage cheat sheet: Argon2id first (19 MiB, 2 iterations, parallelism 1 minimum), scrypt, bcrypt (work factor at least 10, 72-byte limit), PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations; RFC 9106 (rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9106.html, September 2021) specifies Argon2 and recommends Argon2id. The search metadata showed the cheat sheet page as an old index, so the numbers must be re-read on the live page.

plan_fact_checks.claim: The Python standard library can run the Week 5 hash comparison offline.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'Python hashlib scrypt pbkdf2_hmac documentation password hashing' (docs.python.org): hashlib documents scrypt and pbkdf2_hmac only; no Argon2 or bcrypt in the result. Argon2id needs a third-party package (argon2-cffi docs returned); package availability in the lab VM was not verified.

plan_fact_checks.claim: The OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 edition is the current API list (used for BOLA, BFLA, mass assignment terminology).
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'OWASP API Security Top 10 new edition 2025 2026 update release' returned the web Top 10:2025 and the GenAI lists but no API-specific page, so a newer API edition could be neither seen nor excluded. The 2023 edition pages (owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0x11-t10/) are the ones verified.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Burp Suite Community is sufficient for the PortSwigger labs of this week.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Query 'Burp Suite Community Edition free download ...' (portswigger.net): Community includes proxy and history, Repeater, Decoder, Sequencer, Comparer and a rate-restricted Intruder demo; project files, the scanner and Burp Collaborator are Professional features. CSRF PoC generation is a Professional feature per the lab text, so forms are written by hand.
